3.8.9.d: पृथिव्यै त्वान्तरिक्षाय त्वा दिवे त्वेति प्रोक्षत्य् एषा ह्य् एषां लोकानां विधृत्यै मीयते त्रिः प्रोक्षति त्रिषत्या हि देवा अथो त्रयो वा इमे लोका एभ्य एवैनां लोकेभ्यः प्रौक्षीद् अन्नं वै यवा ऊर्ग् उदुम्बरो यद् यवमतीभिः प्रोक्षत्य् ऊर्जा वा एतद् अन्नं समर्धयत्य् ऋक्षं वा अमेध्यम् आपो हविर् यद् अवसिञ्चति मेध्यम् एवैनत् करोत्य् ऋक्षं वा अमेध्यं यद् अवस्तृणाति मेध्यम् एवैनत् करोति पितृदेवत्यं वै निखातम् अमेध्यम् अन्यदेवत्यम् अस्याः खलु वा इमा उत्तमार्ध ओषधयो यद् अवस्तृणात्य् अस्या एवैनाम् उत्तमार्धे मिनोत्य् अनिखातैवाभूद् अन्नं वै यवा ऊर्ग् उदुम्बरो यद् यवम् अवास्यत्य् अन्ने वा एतद् ऊर्जं दधाति न ह्य् अन्नम् ऋत ऊर्जो धिनोति नो ह्य् ऊर्ग् ऋते ऽन्नाद् धिनोति नितानस् त्वा मारुतो निहन्त्व् इति मनो वै नितानः प्राणा मारुता मित्रावरुणौ ध्रुवेण धर्मणेति मित्रम् एवैनां दाधार वरुणः कल्पयति विधृत्यै च खलु वा एषां प्रजानां कॢप्त्यै च मीयते मित्रावरुणौ वै देवानां धर्मधारयौ दैवं वा एतद् धर्मम् अदीधरतां यद् औदुम्बरी ब्रह्मवनिं त्वा क्षत्रवनिं पर्यूहामीत्य् आशीर् एवैषा ब्रह्म दृंह क्षत्रं दृंहेत्य् आशिष एवैष परिग्रहो घृतेन द्यावापृथिवी आपृणेति घृतेनैव द्यावापृथिवी व्युनत्त्य् उदरं वै सद ऊर्ग् उदुम्बरो यद् औदुम्बर्य् ऊर्जं वा एतन् मध्यत आत्मनो धत्ते प्रजानां च प्रजापतेर् वा एतद् उदरं यत् सदः प्राजापत्य उद्गाता तस्माद् उद्गातान्वारभते यजमानो वा औदुम्बरी वर्षिष्ठा कार्या वर्ष्मैनं समानानां गमयति विश्वजनस्य छायासीति छदिर् अभिनिदधाति गोत्राद्गोत्राद् धि प्रसर्पन्त्य् उदरं वै सदो यद् अन्येनान्येन संमिनोति तस्माद् उदरम् अन्येनान्येनामेन संतत उदरं वै सदो यद् अनूचीनं मिनुयात् पराचीनं जग्धम् अतीयाद् अथ यत् तिरश्चीनं मिनोति तस्माज् जग्धं सर्वाण्य् अङ्गान्य् अनुवेति प्रजा वा एतत् समीचीनं मिनोति समीचीर् एनं प्रजा अभिसमावर्तते संयात इव स भवति समानं सांकाशिनं कार्यं समाना हीमे प्राणा यं द्विष्यात् तस्याक्ष्णया मिनुयात् प्राणान् अस्य मोहयति प्रमायुको भवति यदि कामयेत वर्षेत् पर्जन्या इति नीचैः सदो मिनुयाद् वृष्टिम् एव नियछति यदि कामयेत न वर्षेत् पर्जन्या इत्य् उच्चैः सदो मिनुयाद् वृष्टिम् एवापाग्रहीन् नवछदिर् अग्निष्टोमे स्यात् तेजसा त्रिवृता संमितं पञ्चदशछदिर् उक्थ्ये पञ्चदशेन वज्रेण संमितं सप्तदशछदिर् अतिरात्रे सप्तदशो वै प्रजापतिः प्राजापत्या रात्रिर् आनुष्टुभी यज्ञक्रतूनाम् एवैषा व्यावृत्तिः प्राचीनवंशं हविर्धानं मिनोत्य् ऊर्ध्वा हि द्यौः प्राचीनवंशम् आग्नीध्रम् ऊर्ध्वं ह्य् अन्तरिक्षं तिरश्चीनवंशं सदस् तिरश्ची हीयं यजुषा हविर्धानं मिनोति निरुक्ता हि द्यौर् यजुषा सदो निरुक्ता हीयम् अयजुषाग्नीध्रम् अनिरुक्तम् इव ह्य् अन्तरिक्षम् अर्धम् आग्नीध्रस्यान्तर्वेदि मिनोत्य् अर्धं बहिर्वेद्य् अर्धं ह्य् अन्तरिक्षस्यास्मिंल् लोके ऽर्धम् अमुष्मिन् ॥
3.8.9.m: "For the earth, you; / for the intermediate space, you; / for the sky, you," he says as he sprinkles. / For this [post] is set up to support these worlds. / Three times he sprinkles, / for the gods are threefold true. / Moreover, three indeed are these worlds; / for these worlds he has sprinkled it. / Barley is indeed food; / the udumbara is sap. / When he sprinkles with [waters] containing barley, / he thus enriches food with sap. / Bare indeed is impure; / water is an oblation. / When he pours down [water], / he thus makes it pure. / Bare indeed is impure. / When he strews [grass] below, / he thus makes it pure. / What is buried indeed has the fathers as its deity, is impure, and has other deities [as its masters]. / These plants indeed are upon the uppermost part of this [earth]. / When he strews [grass] below, / he sets it up on the uppermost part of this [earth]; / it has become as if not buried at all. / Barley is indeed food; / the udumbara is sap. / When he throws in barley, / he thus places sap in food. / For food does not satisfy without sap, / nor does sap satisfy without food. / "May Nitāna, belonging to the Maruts, strike you down," [he says]; / Nitāna is the mind; / those belonging to the Maruts are the vital breaths. / "Mitra and Varuṇa with firm law," [he says]; / Mitra supports it, Varuṇa disposes it. / Indeed, it is set up both for the support and for the proper arrangement of these offspring. / Mitra and Varuṇa are the upholders of law among the gods; / they two have upheld this divine law. / When [he sets up the post] made of udumbara wood, / "Endowed with the sacred power, endowed with the royal power, I heap earth around you," [he says]; / this is a prayer. / "Strengthen the sacred power, strengthen the royal power," [he says]; / this is the enclosure of the prayer. / "Fill heaven and earth with ghee," [he says]; / with ghee he moistens heaven and earth. / The sadas is indeed the belly; / the udumbara is sap. / Since it is made of udumbara wood, / he thus places sap in the middle of himself and of offspring. / This sadas is the belly of Prajāpati; / the Udgātṛ belongs to Prajāpati; / therefore the Udgātṛ holds on [to it]. / The post of udumbara wood is the sacrificer. / It should be made the highest; / he causes him to reach the highest place among his equals. / "You are the shade of all folk," [he says, and] puts on the roof; / for they creep forward family by family. / The sadas is indeed the belly; / when he sets [it] up with various [materials], / therefore the belly is covered inside with various raw [matters]. / The sadas is indeed the belly; / if he were to set it up lengthwise, what is eaten would pass out away [undigested]. / But when he sets it up crosswise, / therefore what is eaten spreads through all the limbs. / He thus sets it up facing toward the offspring; / the offspring turn toward him all together; / he becomes one who has set out together [with them]. / It should be made uniform, providing a view [throughout]; / for these vital breaths are uniform. / For one whom he hates, he should set it up diagonally; / he confuses his vital breaths; / he becomes prone to die. / If he should desire, "May Parjanya rain," he should set up the sadas low; / he holds down the rain. / If he should desire, "May Parjanya not rain," he should set up the sadas high; / he has held back the rain. / It should have nine roofs at the Agniṣṭoma, / commensurate with the trivṛt [stoma] through fiery energy. / It should have fifteen roofs at the Ukthya, / commensurate with the fifteenfold thunderbolt. / It should have seventeen roofs at the Atirātra; / Prajāpati is seventeenfold; / the night belongs to Prajāpati, being of the Anuṣṭubh meter; / this is the distinction of the sacrificial rites. / He sets up the Havirdhāna with its beams pointing east, / for the sky is upright. / [He sets up] the Āgnīdhra with its beams pointing east, / for the intermediate space is upright. / [He sets up] the sadas with its beams pointing crosswise, / for this [earth] is crosswise. / With a yajus he sets up the Havirdhāna, / for the sky is distinct. / With a yajus [he sets up] the sadas, / for this [earth] is distinct. / Without a yajus [he sets up] the Āgnīdhra, / for the intermediate space is as it were indistinct. / He sets up half of the Āgnīdhra within the altar and half outside the altar, / for half of the intermediate space is in this world / and half in yonder world.
